neighbours.label: The noun that completes a figurative framing of a situation (a vicious circle, another world, a giant experiment, the Age of X); quiet for the same nouns used literally
fire: Debt and low wages keep many workers caught in a vicious cycle.
Stepping into the old library felt like entering a different world.
By burning coal at this rate we are running a vast uncontrolled experiment on the atmosphere.
Critics describe the decade as the Age of Cheap Credit.
The missing letter turned out to be the last piece of the jigsaw.
Rising rents and falling incomes have created a perfect storm.
For the young actors the tour opened a door onto another universe.
Each failed reform pushed the country further into a downward spiral.
quiet: The children rode in a circle around the yard on their bikes.
The old library holds maps from every part of the world.
The class did an experiment with vinegar and baking soda.
He retired at the age of sixty and moved to the coast.
She bought a jigsaw with a thousand pieces for her nephew.
The storm brought down two trees on our street.
The carpenter fitted a new door at the back of the theatre.
The staircase rises in a tight spiral to the bell tower.

notes: Card: ' world', ' circle', ' window', ' experiment', ' Age', ' puzzle', all metaphorical. Probe was weak: 'vicious circle' 0.40, 'another world' 0.14, 'pieces of the puzzle' 0.14, 'Golden Age' 0.14, 'window of opportunity' 0.05; literal uses 0.01-0.02. Probably fails on the median.
